summary:
Visitors to Nord-Est fall under the national framework of Italy. Rules on entry, identity documents, legal gender recognition and criminal law are national and are set out in the country record for Italy; the region-level material identified for Nord-Est concerns Veneto.

The Veneto Regional Council passed motion n.340 at its 178th public session in Venice on 3 July. Deliberation n.92 of 14 October 2014 approved that motion, committing the regional government to a mandatory 'Natural Family Day' observance on the last school day before Christmas and rejecting the aims of gender-awareness content.

The full text of the motion is carried in the official bulletin of the Veneto regional government, which is the primary source for the act; the deliberation is the instrument through which the regional administration was committed.

The measure is educational in scope. It governs a school observance and the regional government's stated position on gender-awareness teaching inside Veneto, and creates no requirement for visitors. No Veneto or other Nord-Est provision on documents, facilities or health-care access appears in this inventory.

The inventory holds no region-specific material for other parts of Nord-Est, and none on regional policing or enforcement practice. For those areas the national assessment for Italy applies without regional qualification.
tangentialFactors:
Measures of this kind record the political posture of a regional administration without creating duties for travellers. The Veneto motion and the deliberation implementing it are the only regional acts documented in this inventory.

Because the inventory contains nothing specific to Nord-Est on health-care access, facility rules or policing, no comparison between Nord-Est and other Italian regions can be drawn from the material here.
localsOnly:
For residents, deliberation n.92 of 14 October 2014 committed the Veneto regional government to a mandatory 'Natural Family Day' on the last school day before Christmas, with the accompanying motion rejecting the aims of gender-awareness content.

The observance is a school-level obligation, so the practical effect falls on pupils and their families and on teaching staff in Veneto, and its content concerns how family and gender are addressed in classrooms.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the Veneto observance adopted in 2014 remains in force is not established by the sources in this inventory; the deliberation and the regional bulletin are the record of its adoption. The year of the council session at which motion n.340 passed is not stated in the source.

The inventory contains no custodial or prison-placement material located in Nord-Est. Documentation of prison placement practice in the inventory concerns institutions elsewhere in Italy and belongs to the country record.

No regional data on anti-trans violence, enforcement, or health-service provision for trans residents in Nord-Est was identified. That absence is a sourcing gap, not evidence that such incidents or services do not exist.
